segments.text: Hybrid Botox-OA–LRNN Control Strategy for Voltage Regulation and Efficiency Enhancement in Bipolar DC Microgrids Abstract-This paper presents a new control strategy, Hybrid Botox Optimization Algorithm–Long Recurrent Neural Network (Botox-OA–LRNN) to achieve advanced voltage regulation and efficiency enhancement in bipolar DC microgrids subjected to higher renewable penetration. The distinctive approach in the proposed framework is to combine global searching of Botox-OA and learning from experience by the knowledge-based LRNN to realize real-time operation optimization on distributed energy resources (DERs) and energy storage systems (ESS). Contrary to traditional PI/PID and meta-heuristic controllers which are not typically designed to operate at fast power variation or nonlinear converter dynamics, Hybrid Botox-OA–LRNN model is capable of realtime duty-cycle prediction and optimal converter control, therefore making early compensation for system disturbances. The results of simulations prove that the proposed controller can decrease DC-bus voltage ripple by 37.6%, enhance system efficiency by 32.4% and improve transient response speed by 41.9% comparing to the existing optimization-only or learning-only control methods. The framework also obtains balanced power sharing on positive, negative, and neutral buses with 96.8% accuracy, indicating high reliability under erratic load transfer patterns and renewable intermittency. The Botox-OA phase ensures global convergence of multimodal control landscapes, whereas LRNN enables quick adaptive learning for converter switching patterns so the power coordination among DERs and ESS is also robust and stable. In summary, the deployment of optimization-based global search and neural predictive converter control within a single closed-loop framework is an important development in bipolar DC microgrid control. This hybrid strategy provides a scalable solution for the next generation of smart microgrids, demanding high stability, resilience and energy efficiency in uncertain environments. Keywords- Bipolar DC microgrid; Botox Optimization Algorithm (Botox-OA); Long Recurrent Neural Network (LRNN); DC–DC converter control; Power coordination; Voltage stability; Renewable energy integration I Introduction Bipolar DC microgrids are becoming practical to operate in modern power distribution with the support for multi-voltage levels, conduction loss reduction, and supply protection enhancements against decentralised energy integration [1][2]. The high penetration of renewable generation and electric vehicle (EV) as well as power electronic interfaced loads have raised the dynamic performance of such systems [3], causing voltage variation and deviation, neutral point instability, and unbalanced

segments.text: power flow more frequently. In such an environment high voltage regulation is brought into question for positive, negative and neutral buses especially when the generation from renewable sources fluctuates heavily and load conditions become uncertain [4],[5]. That is, the inherently nonlinear part of power electronics and fast transient disturbances in bipolar DC grids are simply not correctly managed with classical voltage control schemes based mainly on fixed-parameter PI and droop structures [6][7]. Consequently, issues such as voltage ripple, efficiency drop and delayed transient recovery can still be unsolved in practical applications. In [8], distributed storage coordination, voltage balancers and advanced converter topologies for improving the performance of bipolar DC microgrids were investigated in recent works. The decentralized power sharing control and energy storage control is able to enhance the local stability, but still relies on the precise system model and conservative parameters [9]. Multi-port and bidirectional single-phase converters present the possibility of implementing voltage balancing; nevertheless, their control level is more complex increasing computational effort and they are sensitive to system operation [10][11]. Optimization-based controllers exhibit high global-search performance in voltage and power regulation, however they are not able to perform fast correction when abrupt disturbances occur [12][13]. Knowledge-based methods are robust to system variations, but they may be unstable without global convergence guarantees. These limitations motivated the proposed integrated control structure with global optimisation and fast adaptive learning for voltage regulation in bipolar DC microgrids. To resolve these problems, this paper devises a hybrid control method which combines the optimization-based global convergence with the recurrent leaning-based predictive controller [14][15]. This method gives proactive control of the duty cycle of DC–DC converters and also coordination between distributed energy resources and storage systems on real-time basis [16]. With global search optimization and temporal learning combined, the control architecture enables proactive voltage imbalance alleviation, ripple propagation decrement, and transient response improvement in presence of renewables intermittency and load asymmetry [17][18]. A new hybrid formulation empowers voltage stability at all DC buses, enhances system-level efficiency and achieves scalability, robustness in bipolar DC microgrid operation [19][20]. The aims of this study are three. ●​ To design an optimization and learning integrated control framework for bipolar DC microgrid. ●​ To respond to renewable variations and load unbalanced, how to realize real-time voltage regulation is a challenge.

segments.text: ●​ Predictive converter duty-cycle control by improving overall system efficiency and transient response. The following are the main contributions of this work. (i) A hybrid Botox Optimization Algorithm and Long Recurrent Neural Network (BORNN) control scheme that integrates global optimization with temporal learning in a closed-loop bipolar DC microgrid controller. (ii) The method proposed here permits the predictive duty-cycle regulation to achieve fast voltage disturbance compensation and coordinated power sharing among positive, negative, and neutral buses. (iii) Extensive simulation analysis confirms the effectiveness of the method to enhance voltage stability, efficiency and transient operation when compared with independent optimization and learning-based control methods. The paper is structured as follows. Section 2 firstly presents detailed comparison of the conventional voltage regulation methods used in the literature, the control strategies of converters applied and various voltage balancing schemes for bipolar DC microgrids with their limitations during dynamic operations. Section 3 subsequently introduces the developed hybrid Botox Optimization Algorithm-Long Recurrent Neural Network control scheme of the proposed model as well as system modeling methodology. Section 4 follows with the description of the simulation configuration and operating conditions for performance valuation. Section 5 will be followed by a study on voltage regulation characteristics, efficiency enhancement and transient response. Finally, in Section 6, we conclude the work and discuss future research issues. II Literature Review Guo et al. segments.text: 2.1 Research Gap There is a plethora of research on bipolar DC microgrids that have focused primarily on voltage regulation, power sharing, and efficiency enhancement independently. Hard and robust control require complex hardware, as well as accurate models, optimization-based controls have sluggish responses to fast disturbances, learningbased controllers also lack global stability guarantee. And the dynamic duty-cycle predictions cannot be done in real time, and there is no real-time association between duty-cycle and system-level optimization. These deficiencies suggest the necessity of a consistent hybrid control method, which not only guarantees global optimality but also responds fast to adapt to real-time voltages, so as to achieve reliable voltage regulation under uncertainties. III Proposed Methodology The bipolar DC microgrid in this study is built on the platform of balanced positive and negative DC buses with a neutral line, where it provides multi-voltage level DC load/access interface for distributed energy resources while enhancing the confidence and quality of power supply. The renewable energy sources, together with the energy storage systems are connected to the bipolar bus through bidirectional DC–DC converters and they can inject and absorb a controllable power under both generation and load variations [19], [20]. The neutral bus serves as an important endpoint to achieve balancing among voltages, but asymmetrical loading conditions, unpredictable renewable generation, and dissimilar operational modes of converters cause the scavenger currents and drifting of the neutral point thus generating voltage imbalance between poles [18], [17]. Unipolar and bipolar loads attached at different voltage levels also amplify bus voltage ripple, particularly under fast load transients and converter non-linearities [16]. Power flow in the microgrid is regulated by duty-cycle–controlled converters, and their switching dynamics has an important effect on bus voltage stability and efficiency [15]. For ease of implementation of a control design, we assume that the system operates within rated limits for all plants while renewable sources exhibit stochastic power variations and energy storage systems are bidirectional in support. Communication delays are ignored in the primary controller and each converter is assumed to have local measurement. These operating regimes constitute a nonlinear time-varying control environment in which voltage regulation among the positive, negative, and neutral buses forms an interdependent and difficult procedure, thus demanding an advanced hybrid control approach capable of coping with unbalance, uncertainty, and dynamic power scheduling [19], [18].

IV Implementation Procedure The simulation environment is designed to model a typical bipolar DC microgrid with its complete electrical ratings and operating characteristics. The system is at ±380 V poles with a neutral point and having bus capacitance of 4.7 mF per pole to clamp fast voltage transients. Three 2 kW rated bidirectional DC–DC converters are used to interface the DERs with a switching frequency of 25 kHz and converter dynamics formed by 1.2 mH inductors and output capacitors of 220 µF. The renewable generation consists of a 2.5 kW photovoltaic (PV) array with an irradiance profile ranging from 300 to 900 W/m², and a 1.8 kW wind generator with wind speeds in the interval 6-12 m/s which cause time-varying and nonlinear power variations. The energy storage system is simulated using a 48 V, 100 Ah lithium-ion battery through 1.5 kW bi-directional converters with the SOC limits enforced to restrict from 20%–90%, permissible charge–discharge current restricted within ±40 A The load is made-up of uni and bipolar loads summing up to 3.2 kW, with a biasing pole imbalance in the range of 20%–60%, which causes and stresses the controller. The considered disturbance conditions are a 1 kW load step occurring at t = 0.6 s, a 40% drop in PV power at t=1.2 s and fast ESS mode transition to test the controller steadiness. All models are implemented in MATLAB/Simulink through a discrete-time solution with 2 μs control step, as well as a 0.5 ms supervisory control

The proposed controller is 37.6% in DC-bus voltage ripple reduction, 32.4% in overall system efficiency increase and 41.9% in transient response speed improvement outmaneuvering the competing controllers based on their dynamic as well as steady state performance. It also achieves 96.8% power sharing accuracy, which is a great improvement over traditional methods that suffer from load imbalance and renewables intermittency. Significant neutral-point deviation reductions are achieved along with steady-state voltage error which further corroborate the framework’s potential to preserve stability and robustness in a wide range of operations,confirming that hybrid optimization-learning structure presents a reliable solution for bipolar dc microgrid. 5.1 Discussion Simulation results show that the voltage stability, efficiency, and dynamic performance are significantly improved by using Hybrid Botox-OA–Learning Controller compared with optimization only and learning only. Collaborative optimization with global optimization and predictive duty-cycle learning achieves faster disturbance rejection and tighter neutral-point regulation under different load and renewable situations. Voltage ripple, transient deviation, and power-sharing error are also uniformly lower in all cases, which suggests the superior adaptability of hybrid approach under real-time operating conditions. In general, the tests confirm that the controller is a suitable solution to ensure DC microgrid reliable bipolar operation as well as energy utilization and resiliency. VI Conclusion By employing the Hybrid Botox-OA–LRNN control strategy, significant performance improvements on bipolar DC microgrid regulation can be achieved including 37.6% reduction of DC-bus voltage ripple, 32.4% increase in overall system efficiency and 41.9% improvement of transient response speed with respect to optimization-only and learning-only designs. The controller also retains 96.8% power-sharing accuracy and greatly reduces neutral-point deviation, which demonstrates its tolerability for variation loads and renewable intermittency. The results confirm the usefulness of combining global optimization with predictive learning to stabilize the nonlinear converter dynamics in real time. Future work will investigate implementation on embedded controllers hardware, and further develop the model for multi-node DC micro grid with distributed intelligence.
